questions.q: Using the Kronecker product formula, what is |0⟩ ⊗ |1⟩, where |0⟩ = [1,0] and |1⟩ = [0,1]?
questions.explain: The formula multiplies each entry of |0⟩ by the whole vector |1⟩: the first entry (1) gives block [0,1], the second entry (0) gives block [0,0]; stacking them gives [0,1,0,0], matching the basis vector |01⟩.

questions.q: For an m x m matrix A tensored with an n x n matrix B, what are the dimensions of the resulting matrix A ⊗ B?
options: The same m by m dimensions as A alone
m by n, a non-square matrix
questions.explain: The Kronecker product arranges m x m blocks, each of which is itself an n x n matrix, producing an (mn) x (mn) result -- consistent with the dimension-multiplying rule from the previous lesson.

questions.q: When building X ⊗ I block by block (X = Pauli-X, I = 2x2 identity), what is block (1,2) of the resulting 4x4 matrix, and why?
options: A 1x1 scalar, because tensor product blocks are always single numbers
The zero matrix [[0,0],[0,0]], because X12 is always 0
The 2x2 identity matrix [[1,0],[0,1]], because block (1,2) equals X's entry X12 = 1 multiplied by the entire matrix I
The Pauli-X matrix itself, because blocks always copy X regardless of position
questions.explain: Block (i,j) of A tensor B is always Aij times the full matrix B. Since X12 = 1, block (1,2) is 1 times I, which is just I itself: [[1,0],[0,1]].

questions.q: Why are X ⊗ I and I ⊗ X different 4x4 matrices even though both are built from the same two 2x2 matrices?
options: I ⊗ X is always the zero matrix by definition
They are actually always identical matrices; the lesson's distinction is only a notational convention with no numeric effect

Tensor product order encodes which subsystem (qubit) each operator acts on -- X ⊗ I flips qubit 1 and leaves qubit 2 alone, while I ⊗ X does the opposite, so swapping operand order changes the physical operation and the resulting matrix
X ⊗ I only applies to vectors, never to matrices, so the comparison is invalid
questions.explain: The tensor product is not commutative in general: which operator sits in the 'first qubit' slot vs. the 'second qubit' slot determines which qubit gets acted on, producing genuinely different matrices.

questions.q: Why is attempting to compute A ⊗ B by ordinary matrix multiplication (A times B) a mistake?
options: Matrix multiplication and the Kronecker product always give the exact same numeric answer, so it doesn't matter which one you use
The Kronecker product is simply another name for matrix multiplication
Matrix multiplication is only valid for vectors, never for matrices

Ordinary matrix multiplication produces a different-sized result (or is undefined unless sizes happen to match) and follows a completely different rule than the Kronecker product's block-construction method
questions.explain: A x B (ordinary multiplication) requires matching inner dimensions and produces a result with different dimensions than A ⊗ B, which is always (mn) x (mn) regardless of whether ordinary multiplication would even be defined -- they are distinct operations.
